sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Youngstown, Ohio?
sections.html:
Youngstown is the Mahoning County seat and the largest of the four Ohio cities in this comparison, with 58,832 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. That is down 2.0% from the April 2020 estimates base of 60,049 and well below the 66,982 counted in 2010. Selling here means working with a market shaped by the steel era, a smaller population than the city was built for, and a lot of older housing.

The city grew around coal, iron and then steel mills along the Mahoning River. Wikipedia notes that local ore ran out early in the twentieth century and that mills had to bring ore in by rail, which put Youngstown at a cost disadvantage and started its manufacturing decline earlier than in some other cities. The effects are still visible in the housing stock and the tax base.

Youngstown became the county seat in 1876, when the seat moved from Canfield. The county auditor's offices, the courthouse and most of the records you need for a sale are in the city.

sections.h2: How do Youngstown home values and incomes compare?
sections.html:
Prices are a different scale from the other cities in the table. Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 lists a median owner-occupied value of $63,300, a median gross rent of $728 and 56.2% owner-occupied homes among 24,982 households. Median household income is $34,408, and 37.3% of residents are in poverty.

  • Median selected monthly owner costs are $916 with a mortgage and $379 without, the lowest of the four cities.
  • The city is 41.4% White alone and 40.4% Black alone, with 12.3% Hispanic or Latino residents.
  • The largest employer in the city is Youngstown State University, which serves about 11,000 students.

Health care is the largest of the sectors QuickFacts lists: about $1.32 billion in 2022 receipts for health care and social assistance, compared with $418.5 million in retail sales. Youngstown's other major employers include Vallourec Star Steel in Brier Hill and Trivium Packaging.

sections.h2: Which Youngstown neighborhoods do buyers and investors ask about?
sections.html:
Wikipedia divides the city into downtown, a North Side, a South Side and other districts. Downtown holds government buildings, banks and venues such as the Covelli Centre and Powers Auditorium, with Youngstown State University and the Butler Institute of American Art just to the north. The North Side includes Brier Hill, Crandall Park, North Heights and Wick Park, where industrial executives built mansions that still stand in historic districts. Brier Hill hosts a festival at the end of every August.

The South Side is the densest and most populous part of the city and includes Oak Hill, Erie, Warren and Lower Gibson. Interstate 680 serves the city directly and connects to I-80, the Ohio Turnpike and State Route 11. State Route 711 runs north, and the Madison Avenue and Himrod Avenue expressways form a freeway loop around downtown.

The Youngstown City School District covers almost all of the city and has been under state oversight since 2015. Wikipedia reports that the graduation rate rose from 65% in 2015 to 88% in 2020. Catholic and private schools within the city include Cardinal Mooney High School and Ursuline High School.

sections.h2: What must a Youngstown landlord or owner register with the city?
sections.html:
Registration is the Youngstown rule that surprises sellers most. Under Section 546.11 of the city's Codified Ordinances, every rental property must be registered and licensed annually, other than public housing and Section 8 units, which follow federal inspection rules. The city's Property Code Enforcement and Demolition page adds that, except for owner-occupied homes, all properties must now be registered.

  • The fee is $40 for a single rental unit. In a multi-unit building it is $40 for the first unit and $25 for each additional unit.
  • An unlicensed rental can be fined $100 for each week it is unlicensed, and criminal penalties are possible.
  • Once the form and fee arrive, a provisional license is issued for one year while an inspection is scheduled within 30 days.
  • If the property fails inspection the owner has 30 days to fix the violations, and each re-inspection costs $40.
  • Cancelling an inspection after 8:00 a.m. on the day costs $25, and later late cancellations cost $100 each.

Vacant properties have their own registration program run by the same office. Before you list a vacant house, call the Property Registration Department at (330) 742-8743 and ask whether the address is registered and whether fees are open. The office keeps weekday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

sections.h2: Can a Youngstown house on the demolition list still be sold?
sections.html:
Ask the city first, because Youngstown decides which houses are condemned. The Mahoning County Land Bank says it works at the request of cities, villages and townships when demolition funds are available, and that local governments decide which houses are condemned. In Youngstown, call the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office at (330) 742-8888 to ask where an address stands.

The Land Bank also answers several questions that come up in sales. It keeps no list of houses it owns and says it had none in inventory to renovate, with renovation programs due to relaunch in 2026. It does not hold owner phone numbers, so a buyer must find the deeded owner through the auditor's property search. It also says the idea of buying a house for $1 is an urban legend.

If a house is torn down, taxes still follow the building for a time. The Mahoning County Auditor says taxes are collected a year behind, so you are still taxed on the building's value if it was standing on January 1 of the tax year being collected. A demolition permit for a Youngstown residence comes from the city's Property Code Enforcement and Demolition Department.

sections.h2: How does Mahoning County set values, and when can you appeal?
sections.html:
Ohio requires each county auditor to reappraise every parcel every six years. Mahoning County completed its reappraisal for tax year 2023, with taxes collected in 2024, and the next reappraisal is for tax year 2030. A triennial update, which studies sales without visiting each property, applies to tax year 2026 with taxes collected in 2027.

An owner who believes the value is too high can file a Complaint Against the Valuation of Real Property between January 2 and March 31 each year. The Board of Revision is made up of the county auditor, the county treasurer and the president of the county commissioners, and it hears evidence on value only. Its address is 120 Market Street in Youngstown, and the auditor's office can be reached at (330) 740-2010. For payment questions, call the county treasurer at (330) 740-2460.

What the Mahoning Board of Revision accepts for residential value complaints
EvidenceDetail printed by the auditor
Recent saleClosing statement, purchase agreement and conveyance statement for a sale within 24 months, with a notarized arm's-length affidavit
ListingA listing agreement if the property is currently for sale
AppraisalA report by a certified appraiser for tax valuation, subject to review
ConditionPhotographs with professional repair estimates
New constructionBuilder-certified costs for work five years old or less

The auditor adds that tax increases themselves are not a ground for a value complaint, because taxes result from voted levies.

sections.h2: What does Ohio require a Youngstown seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires the property disclosure form for most sales of one to four unit homes. It does not apply to a transfer by a foreclosure sale, a deed in lieu of foreclosure, a transfer ordered by a court, or a transfer by a fiduciary administering an estate. If you are selling as an estate fiduciary or after a court order, confirm which exception applies to you.

The city also publishes a Property Transfer Affidavit, listed among the forms on its code enforcement page. Ask the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office whether your sale needs one and what it must say before you schedule a closing.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer make sense for a Youngstown house?
sections.html:
A cash offer makes sense when the cost of repair, a rental license problem or a vacant-property registration issue would hold up a conventional buyer's financing. A lender's appraiser and inspector will look closely at a house with roof, plumbing or foundation problems, and the low median values here leave little cushion.

Compare more than one offer, ask who pays closing costs, and get the closing date in writing. Ask the title company to send the settlement statement ahead of time so you can confirm any unpaid city fees or taxes are deducted from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental before I sell a Youngstown house?
faqs.a: If the house is rented, the city says it must be registered and licensed annually, and an unlicensed rental can be fined $100 for each week. Call the Property Registration Department at (330) 742-8743 to confirm the status of your address before closing.

faqs.q: What if my Youngstown house is vacant and on the demolition list?
faqs.a: Call the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office at (330) 742-8888. The Mahoning County Land Bank says local governments decide which houses are condemned and that it acts on their requests when funding is available.

faqs.q: When do I file a value complaint in Mahoning County?
faqs.a: File between January 2 and March 31. The auditor's page says complaints for tax year 2026 begin January 2, 2027, and mail or in-person filing goes to the Board of Revision at 120 Market Street.

faqs.q: Is there a disclosure exemption for estate sales in Youngstown?
faqs.a: Yes. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 exempts a transfer by a fiduciary in the course of administering a decedent's estate and a court-ordered transfer, among others.

faqs.q: Will I still pay tax on a Youngstown house I demolish?
faqs.a: Yes for the year in question. The county auditor says taxes are collected a year behind, so a building that stood on January 1 of the tax year is taxed on that year's value even after demolition.
